analysis: Both changed files are XCTest/Testing sources only; no production code, wire protocol, key handling, attestation, cache storage, or authorization path changes. EngineV2MTPProductionAdmissionTests.swift line 153 now qualifies the decoder type as MLXLLM.Gemma4TextConfiguration, a compile-time disambiguation with no runtime security effect. The test file itself is gated behind DARKBLOOM_EXCLUSIVE_NATIVE_GPU_TEST for native-construction cases and uses synthetic fixture keys (line 380, explicitly no keychain) and temporary directories that are cleaned up, so it does not touch real KEK material or the encrypted prefix cache (T-041 posture unchanged). MTPResliceFallbackTests.swift line 81 updates the test-double LanguageModel.prepare signature to (input, cache, state: LMOutput.State?, prefill: PrefillParameters), which reflects an upstream mlx-swift-lm protocol change. The double returns .tokens(input.text) and is test-only. The conformance change implies a dependency or API bump elsewhere in the PR, which was not supplied here. Whether that bump changes prefill or state semantics in production providers (T-028, TB-007) cannot be judged from these units. The real security-relevant integration question is to check that the dependency update and the production LanguageModel conformances behave correctly, including prefill and cache handling. No findings are raised from the supplied evidence.
